Think a guilty verdict is the end of the road? Think again. 🤔 Trial judges make procedural mistakes, prosecutors sometimes overstep their authority, and defense attorneys occasionally miss protecting critical rights. When that happens, a criminal appeal or post-conviction motion gives you a genuine second chance to challenge those errors and protect your freedom.

Appeals in Florida don't re-try your case or bring in new witnesses. Instead, an appellate attorney carefully reviews your entire trial record to spot legal errors that hurt your defense or led to an unlawful sentence. Common issues include improperly admitted evidence, confrontation clause violations, flawed expert testimony, and even translation errors, a real problem in our diverse Miami community. Immigration issues also matter, especially if your lawyer didn't advise you about deportation risks before you accepted a plea deal.

The clock is ticking though. Direct appeals must be filed within 30 days of your sentence, while post-conviction motions under Florida Rule 3.850 have a two-year deadline from when your conviction becomes final. ⚖️

Learn more about how our appellate team builds focused strategies to challenge trial errors and give you a real second chance.

ownerUpdates/6/text:
Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.

Before you assume “it wasn’t even a real car,” talk to an experienced DUI lawyer.

ownerUpdates/6/text:
Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.

Before you assume “it wasn’t even a real car,” talk to an experienced DUI lawyer.

My husband was just diagnosed with terminal cancer that had metastasized into the bone.  Medically, I knew that time was short for him.  Our living trust needed updating, since it was set up in 2004, but we had been procrastinating doing an update for the past two years.

I could not contact my attorney, who prepared the original trust, will, and durable power of attorney, and asked my daughter, who lives in California to find someone else.  Time was of the essence since my husband had just entered hospice care and was rapidly declining in health.

My daughter found Isabel after searching for estate lawyers near me who had received strong reviews.  When she called, Isabel was in a conference, but promised to call and discuss my situation during a break.  After my daughter explained my urgent need, Isabel expedited a meeting with my daughter and me, as soon as my daughter flew into Florida. To speed things up, Isabel had my daughter FedEx the 2004 documents to her, so Isabel could familiarize herself with the documents and identify what changes were needed to meet current legal requirements.

My daughter and I met Isabel early in the morning.  Isabel expressed several concerns that she had about the 2004 documents.  She was very methodical and precise with every detail, and the reasoning behind the suggested changes, including the need to have a living will.

I felt the same sense of confidence and trust in Isabel as my daughter experienced during her initial telephone call.  I was perfectly comfortable communicating my husband's and my wishes to Isabel.  I felt that I was in extremely capable hands and that our wishes would be fulfilled.  Because of my urgency,

Isabel prioritized the update, and asked me to return in the afternoon to review, and to sign my updated documents.  She also explained that she wanted to have my husband sign his documents by the next day, but since he was bedridden, that she would participate via telephone, while a notary and two witnesses sat with my husband to witness his understanding and signing of the updated documents.

When I returned in the afternoon, Isabel walked me through the updated documents and had my documents signed by me in front of two witnesses and a notary.  Then, in testimony to her thoroughness, she asked if my husband and I had prepared health care surrogate designations.  When I gave her our 2004 versions, she again noted that significant changes in law had occurred, and updated versions were needed.  She asked me to stay for a short time, while she prepared new versions.  Then Isabel had me sign in front of the witnesses and the notary.

The next day, by telephone, Isabel held the review and witnessed signings for my husband's documents.  Once again, Isabel was meticulous in making sure that my husband understood what documents he was signing, verbally guiding my husband, the witnesses, and the notary through each step requiring a witnessed signature, and verifying that proper identifications were produced.

I can literally go on and on noting the above and beyond work that Isabel took upon herself to make sure that the updated trust was exactly what my husband and I wanted.

Truly, what separates Isabel from all other trust attorneys is not only her in-depth knowledge and precision for detail, but her kindness and spirit radiating from within.    You know that she is doing this from her heart.

I can't think of another professional that I would feel honored to write a review about, and I hope that this review truly captures what an amazing woman and attorney Isabel Bettancourt-Levey is.

Fran B.

Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.

Before you assume “it wasn’t even a real car,” talk to an experienced DUI lawyer.

If you are Israeli, I am especially disappointed that you chose to try to harm the reputation of another Israeli-owned business when, by your own description, you were not seeking a legal service or representation that our firm provides.

Our website clearly explains that our consultations are offered free of charge to people who have a legal case that our firm handles, with the expectation that, after receiving legal advice about their options, they may choose to retain us.

A consultation that is solely for general information, where there is no case for our firm to handle, is different. In that situation, you are paying for the attorney's time, education, experience, overhead, and legal analysis—just as you would pay a doctor, psychologist, accountant, or other professional for their time. In fact, many law firms charge for an initial consultation even when the person does have a case.

For more than 22 years, we have been generous in offering complimentary consultations to prospective clients whose cases fall within our practice and that we can actually handle. That does not mean that every person seeking general legal information is entitled to unlimited free legal advice.

As you described in your review, you were advised regarding your situation and were told that it was not a matter our firm could take on. You were therefore not a client of our firm. I find it unfair that, after receiving an appropriate explanation, you chose to post a negative review against a lawyer and law firm with whom you never established an attorney-client relationship.

Our website does not state that every person, regardless of circumstances, receives a free legal consultation. The free consultation is for prospective clients with cases that we handle. If you already filed a matter, or if your situation falls outside the cases we take, a paid consultation may be required.

Our firm is a substantial law office with many employees and significant operating expenses. A consultation fee is simply compensation for the attorney's professional time and resources. It is not reasonable to expect a law firm to provide professional legal analysis for free when there is no potential legal matter for the firm to handle.

I respectfully ask that, since you were never our client, you remove the review. A review should accurately reflect an actual client experience with the services provided by the business—not a disagreement over a consultation policy that was clearly explained to you.

I hope, as a fellow Israeli and as a business owner or professional yourself, you can understand the difference between a legitimate client complaint and a negative review from someone who was not a client and was seeking information about a matter we do not handle.

First, we always have staff answering our phones and responding to emails. Like every busy law firm, there may occasionally be delays, but we have employees dedicated to client communication every day.

Second, your statement that our firm charged approximately $35,000 is false. We have no case that comes anywhere close to that amount. That statement alone calls into question the accuracy of your entire review.

Our attorneys have many years of immigration experience and have handled hundreds, and often thousands, of immigration cases. We do not hire inexperienced attorneys to represent clients in complex removal proceedings.

Immigration court is one of the most difficult areas of law. No attorney can guarantee success. The outcome depends on the facts, the client's testimony, the law, the government, and ultimately the Immigration Judge's discretion.

Asylum approval rates have always varied dramatically by judge, court, and presidential administration. Some judges have historically granted over 80% of asylum cases, while the national approval rate has been much lower. Changes in approval rates reflect changes in government policy and judicial discretion—not whether attorneys suddenly became good or bad.

Our firm continues to win many extremely difficult cases. In fact, today we won a very challenging EOIR 42B Cancellation of Removal case that could just as easily have been denied depending on the evidence and the judge's exercise of discretion. That is simply the reality of litigation.

Personally, I passed the bar examination among the top candidates in the country and have devoted my career exclusively to immigration law for more than two decades. Our firm has successfully represented thousands of immigrants and earned hundreds of five-star reviews.

False factual statements that harm a person's or business's reputation may constitute defamation under Florida law. See, for example, Florida Statutes Chapter 770 regarding libel actions, as well as Florida common law governing defamation. This review reflects my personal experience and opinions, and is supported by the allegations and dates set out in my publicly filed civil complaint in Broward County.

I retained Attorney Fallon Zirpoli as part of my criminal-defense team. What I needed was conflict‑free, diligent, and transparent advocacy. What I experienced instead was a pattern that—based on my documentation—undermined those fundamentals.

Conflicts and nondisclosure. When I asked directly about ties to a key adverse witness, Ms. Zirpoli denied any connection. I later discovered (and pleaded) that she had an academic affiliation that should have been disclosed (a Nova Law Review tie). In my view, that was a material relationship that raised a significant risk of a “material limitation” and required full disclosure and my informed consent before the representation continued. The denial and omission are specifically identified by date in my complaint.

Candor and communication. My complaint details that major strategic choices affecting impeachment and context were made without my informed consent—including decisions that curtailed the use of impeachment/exculpatory material and kept crucial family‑court background from the jury. Even when filings bore co‑counsel’s name, Ms. Zirpoli did not correct course, ensure my objectives were honored, or secure written consent for significant limitations. Those omissions, in my view, breached the basic duties of loyalty, candor, and communication I was owed.

Why this matters to you. Criminal cases turn on credibility and independence of counsel. A lawyer must disclose personal/professional ties that could color judgment, obtain your informed consent in writing for conflicted or limiting decisions, and communicate frankly about risks and tradeoffs. My experience with Ms. Zirpoli fell short on those points, as laid out with dates, places, and supporting facts in my complaint.

Impact. The combination of nondisclosure and unilateral strategic limits caused concrete harm: additional legal expense, reputational damage, and a materially weaker defense than a conflict‑free, fully informed strategy would have provided. Those consequences are set out in the pleading and are the basis for my claims for breach of fiduciary duty, fraudulent concealment/constructive fraud, and negligent misrepresentation as to her conduct.

Bottom line. If you value independence, transparency, and client‑first judgment, I cannot recommend Attorney Fallon Zirpoli. In my opinion, her handling of conflicts and client communication did not meet the standard I expected or the duties described in my complaint. Prospective clients should ask very direct questions about potential relationships with witnesses or opposing counsel and demand written conflict disclosures and consent before proceeding.

Florida is rapidly pulling back from FLOCK cameras and automated license plate readers.

Following action by Gov. Ron DeSantis and FDOT to remove ALPR cameras from State Highway System rights-of-way, counties, sheriffs and cities across Florida are reviewing their own programs. Some have already suspended use, terminated contracts or announced camera removals.

But calling it a statewide "ban" isn't accurate. Rules vary by jurisdiction, and privately operated cameras may remain.

We've created a Florida FLOCK Camera Tracker showing the latest county-by-county restrictions and announcements.

Read the full tracker to see what's happening in your area.

ownerUpdates/9/text:
Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.

Before you assume “it wasn’t even a real car,” talk to an experienced DUI lawyer.

🏍️ Accidente de Motocicleta en Florida: Lo Que Debe Saber

Del 15 al 18 de octubre llega Biketoberfest y las carreteras de Florida se llenan de motociclistas. Antes de rodar, entienda algo clave: las motocicletas están excluidas del sistema PIP de Florida.

⚠️ El PIP sin culpa no cubre a los motociclistas lesionados
🛡️ Su recuperación depende del seguro del otro conductor o de su propia cobertura contra conductores sin seguro
⏳ El plazo para demandar por negligencia en Florida es de dos años, no cuatro
🪖 No usar casco no elimina su derecho a reclamar
📸 Fotos, testigos e informe policial deciden casos
🚫 No dé declaraciones grabadas a la aseguradora contraria sin asesoría

El escenario más común sigue siendo el automóvil que gira a la izquierda frente a una moto que venía de frente. Casi siempre la responsabilidad es del automóvil, pero la aseguradora va a intentar culparlo a usted.

ownerUpdates/1/text:
⚖️ Resbalón y Caída en Florida: Lo Que Debe Probar

Caerse en una tienda no basta para ganar un caso en Florida. La ley le exige probar algo que el negocio controla: lo que el negocio sabía.

📋 El estándar. Cuando la caída es por una sustancia transitoria en un comercio, usted debe demostrar conocimiento real o constructivo. Real es que alguien del negocio lo sabía. Constructivo es que la condición llevaba suficiente tiempo ahí como para que debieran haberla descubierto.

🎥 La evidencia desaparece. Los videos de seguridad se sobrescriben en días o semanas. Las bitácoras de limpieza existen pero nadie las preserva por iniciativa propia. Por eso enviamos cartas de preservación de evidencia de inmediato.

📱 El mismo día: reporte la caída y pida copia del reporte, fotografíe la sustancia, el piso y su calzado, anote testigos, y busque atención médica.

⏳ El plazo ahora es de dos años, no cuatro, para accidentes después del 24 de marzo de 2023. En propiedad pública los plazos de aviso son mucho más cortos.

⚠️ Negligencia comparativa al 51 por ciento. Si le atribuyen más del 50 por ciento de culpa, no recupera nada.

El ajustador va a llamar y va a sonar amable. Hable con un abogado primero. Consulta gratis.
ownerUpdates/2/text:
⚖️ Homicidio Culposo en Florida: Lo Que Toda Familia Debe Saber

Perder a un familiar por la negligencia de otra persona deja preguntas que nadie quiere hacerse todavía. Aquí está lo esencial, en claro.

📌 Es un caso civil, separado del caso penal. Si la fiscalía no presenta cargos, su familia todavía puede tener un caso válido — el estándar de prueba civil es más bajo.

👤 En Florida la familia no presenta la demanda directamente. La presenta el representante personal del patrimonio. Sin testamento, un tribunal debe nombrarlo, lo que significa abrir una sucesión junto con la demanda.

💵 Se puede reclamar apoyo económico perdido, pérdida de compañía y orientación, sufrimiento mental del cónyuge e hijos menores, y gastos médicos y funerarios.

⏳ El plazo general es de dos años desde el fallecimiento. Los casos contra entidades del gobierno exigen avisos formales en plazos mucho más cortos.

🚫 No firme nada de una aseguradora antes de hablar con un abogado.

Manejamos la demanda civil y la sucesión bajo un mismo techo, en español e inglés. Si no hay recuperación, no hay honorarios.
ownerUpdates/3/text:
🚶 Atropellado en Miami? Esto Es Lo Que Debe Saber

Septiembre es uno de los meses más peligrosos del año para caminar o andar en bicicleta en el sur de la Florida: las clases empezaron, hay más niños en las calles y oscurece más temprano justo a la hora de salida del trabajo.

Hasta mayo de 2026, Florida ya registraba 204 muertes de peatones y 56 de ciclistas en el año.

Si lo atropellan:

🚑 Llame al 911 y acepte la evaluación médica, aunque se sienta bien
📋 Asegúrese de que exista reporte policial y pida el número
📸 Fotos del lugar, del vehículo, de la bicicleta, de la iluminación y de sus lesiones
👥 Nombres y teléfonos de testigos antes de que se vayan
🤐 No dé declaraciones grabadas a la aseguradora del conductor

Dato que casi nadie sabe: su propio seguro de auto puede cubrirlo aunque usted iba a pie o en bicicleta, y la cobertura de conductor sin seguro suele ser la fuente de recuperación más importante en atropellos graves. Si el conductor se dio a la fuga, el caso no está perdido.

El plazo en Florida es de dos años, y los reclamos contra una ciudad o condado tienen plazos de notificación mucho más cortos.

Somos un bufete de juicio. Hablamos español, atendemos 24/7, usted habla directamente con su abogado y la consulta es gratis.

Guía completa 👇
ownerUpdates/4/text:
⚖️ ¿Un Socio, un Contrato o una Propiedad en Disputa?

No todos los problemas legales empiezan con un accidente. Muchos empiezan con una firma.

Un socio que deja de cumplir. Un contratista que abandona la obra a mitad del trabajo. Un inquilino comercial que no paga. Un contrato que la otra parte interpreta de una manera muy conveniente para ella.

📄 Incumplimiento de contrato
🤝 Disputas entre socios de negocio
🏢 Conflictos de bienes raíces y arrendamientos comerciales
💰 Cobro de deudas y pagarés
🚩 Fraude y tergiversación
👨‍👩‍👧 Disputas de herencia entre familiares

Lo primero que debe confirmar es su plazo. La Florida tiene términos de prescripción estrictos, y no son iguales para un contrato escrito, uno verbal o un reclamo por fraude. Muchos esperan a ver si el problema se resuelve solo, y cuando finalmente consultan, la puerta ya se cerró.

Lo segundo: guarde todo. Contratos, facturas, correos, mensajes de texto, fotos. Los litigios civiles se ganan con documentación, no con memoria.

La mayoría de estos casos se resuelven antes del juicio. Pero usted obtiene un buen acuerdo precisamente porque la otra parte cree que usted está listo para litigar. Un bufete que nunca va a juicio negocia desde la debilidad.

Despacho boutique. Usted habla directamente con su abogado. Consulta gratuita, 24/7, y hablamos español.

Guía completa sobre litigios civiles en Florida 👇
ownerUpdates/5/text:
⚖️ Falleció un ser querido y hay bienes en Miami: ¿y ahora qué?

Cuando una persona fallece en Florida y deja una casa o una cuenta bancaria solo a su nombre, la familia descubre rápido que nada se mueve sin una orden judicial. A ese proceso se le llama probate o sucesión, y entenderlo temprano evita meses de retraso.

📄 Florida ofrece dos caminos principales: la administración sumaria, para patrimonios pequeños o fallecimientos de hace más de dos años, y la administración formal, que suele tomar de seis meses a un año y requiere el nombramiento de un representante personal.

🏠 La vivienda principal tiene una protección especial llamada homestead, que normalmente la resguarda de los acreedores generales, pero que casi siempre exige un trámite judicial antes de poder vender o refinanciar.

✅ Si no hay testamento, la ley decide quién hereda, y rara vez coincide con lo que la familia esperaba. Y si los herederos viven fuera del país, no hace falta viajar: los documentos se firman con apostilla y nosotros comparecemos ante el tribunal.

Atendemos familias en Miami, North Miami, Hollywood y Tallahassee, en español y en inglés, con consulta inicial gratuita y disponibilidad 24/7. No le huimos a los abusadores.
ownerUpdates/6/text:
🌧️ Temporada de Lluvias en Miami: Maneja con Cuidado

Agosto trae las tormentas más fuertes del año al sur de Florida, y con ellas más accidentes de tránsito. ⚠️

El hidroplaneo puede ocurrir con apenas una décima de pulgada de agua, a solo 35 mph. Cuando el auto pierde tracción, no puedes frenar ni dirigir. 🚗💨

🌦️ Reduce la velocidad y aumenta la distancia
🛞 Revisa tus neumáticos antes de la temporada
💡 Enciende las luces bajas bajo la lluvia
📸 Si chocas, documenta la escena y busca atención médica

Recuerda: la lluvia no libera a un conductor de su responsabilidad. Quien manejaba demasiado rápido para las condiciones puede ser responsable del accidente —aunque "el clima tuvo la culpa".

Si sufriste un accidente, no enfrentes a las aseguradoras solo. En Gilbert & Smallman hablamos español, te atendemos directamente y ofrecemos consultas gratuitas. 💪
ownerUpdates/7/text:
🚗 Día del Trabajo en Miami: Conozca Sus Derechos en un Punto de Control de DUI

El fin de semana del Día del Trabajo trae más celebraciones… y más operativos policiales contra la conducción bajo los efectos del alcohol. Si conduce en Miami durante el feriado, saber cómo actuar en un punto de control puede marcar toda la diferencia.

Tenga presente lo siguiente:

🛑 Debe detenerse y ser cortés en un control debidamente señalizado
🤐 Tiene derecho a permanecer en silencio ante preguntas que puedan incriminarlo
🚶 Las pruebas de sobriedad de campo son subjetivas: nervios, fatiga o superficies irregulares afectan el resultado
⏱️ Si lo arrestan, tiene solo unos 10 días para proteger su licencia de conducir

Un arresto por DUI no es una condena. En Florida se abren dos procesos a la vez —uno penal y otro por su licencia— y actuar rápido es clave. Un abogado revisará si el control cumplió la ley, si hubo causa probable y si sus derechos fueron respetados.

Nuestro despacho es completamente bilingüe. Usted habla directamente con su abogado, no con un intermediario. No nos dejamos intimidar por los fiscales.

Este feriado, planee con cabeza. Y si algo sale mal, no firme nada sin asesoría. 👇
ownerUpdates/8/text:

En agosto, los autobuses escolares vuelven a las calles de Miami-Dade y Broward, y con ellos aumentan los accidentes. Los momentos más peligrosos ocurren cuando los niños suben o bajan del autobús, en la llamada "zona de peligro", donde el conductor no siempre los ve.

⚖️ Pasar un autobús escolar detenido con las luces rojas encendidas viola la ley de Florida.
🚸 Su familia puede reclamar por gastos médicos, dolor y sufrimiento.
✅ En Gilbert & Smallman investigamos a fondo, reunimos las pruebas y peleamos por los suyos.

No huimos de los abusadores. Hablamos español y ofrecemos consultas gratuitas las 24 horas, los 7 días.
ownerUpdates/9/text:
⚖️ Florida Elimina el Seguro "No-Fault" (PIP) — Esto Le Afecta
Un cambio histórico transformó los accidentes de tránsito en Florida. Desde el 1 de julio de 2026, el estado eliminó el sistema PIP "no-fault" y pasó a un sistema basado en la culpa. Si usted maneja en Miami, esto cambia todo lo que ocurre después de un choque. 🚗

Lo que necesita saber:

⚖️ Ya no depende primero de su propio PIP de $10,000
✅ Ahora el seguro del conductor CULPABLE paga sus gastos médicos y su dolor y sufrimiento
📋 Nuevos mínimos: $25,000 por persona / $50,000 por accidente en lesiones corporales
⏰ El plazo para demandar por negligencia ahora es de 2 años, no 4

¿Por qué importa tanto? Porque responsabilizar correctamente al causante del accidente es más importante que nunca — y las aseguradoras harán todo lo posible por pagar menos. Ahí es donde un abogado marca la diferencia.

En Gilbert & Smallman investigamos la escena, documentamos la culpa y negociamos por usted. Consultas gratuitas, disponibilidad 24/7, y atención en español. No le tenemos miedo a los abusadores. 🙌

No espere: esperar demasiado puede costarle su derecho a ser compensado.

What Happens If You Refuse A Breath Test After A Miami DUI Arrest?

A qualifying refusal can now produce a separate criminal charge in addition to driver's license consequences. A first qualifying refusal of lawful breath or urine testing can be charged as a second-degree misdemeanor, while a qualifying repeat refusal can be charged as a first-degree misdemeanor. A Miami DUI lawyer can examine whether law enforcement complied with the required arrest, testing, and warning procedures. Language barriers, misunderstanding, medical conditions, failed attempts to blow, or unclear instructions may also be relevant depending on what the recordings show.
ownerUpdates/1/text:
Can A Miami DUI Be Reduced To Reckless Driving?

Yes, a Miami DUI can sometimes be resolved as reckless driving, but the result depends on the particular case and negotiations. A Miami DUI attorney can examine whether the traffic stop complied with constitutional requirements, whether probable cause supported the arrest, whether roadside exercises provide persuasive evidence, and whether breath, blood, or urine testing can be challenged. Body-camera footage may also affect the prosecution's assessment of the case. A reduction is not guaranteed based solely on having no prior record. Before agreeing to a plea, defendants should understand all conditions and collateral consequences.
ownerUpdates/2/text:
What Should You Do Immediately After A Miami DUI Arrest?

Begin by preserving every document you received and determining whether your driver's license was administratively suspended. A Miami DUI lawyer can identify the agencies involved and seek body-camera video, dash-camera footage, breath-test documentation, traffic-camera records, surveillance video, and witness information. In a large metropolitan area, third-party video may exist from parking facilities, condominiums, businesses, rideshare vehicles, or nearby properties, but it may not be retained indefinitely. Avoid discussing the arrest publicly or on social media. Prompt investigation can help determine whether objective evidence supports the observations described by law enforcement.
ownerUpdates/3/text:
What Should I Look For When Searching For The Best Miami DUI Lawyer?

Searching for the best Miami DUI lawyer can be difficult because South Florida has many criminal defense attorneys. Start by focusing specifically on DUI experience. Ask how often the attorney handles cases involving breath-test results, refusals, blood testing, field sobriety exercises, drug impairment, crashes, and disputed traffic stops.

Experience handling DUI cases in Miami-Dade County is another factor worth considering.

The attorney should also be prepared to investigate the prosecution’s evidence rather than relying solely on the arrest report. Body-camera recordings, dash-camera footage, breath-testing documentation, witness statements, and other records may provide important information about what happened.

Ask who will personally handle your case and how the firm keeps clients informed.

No attorney should promise that a DUI charge will automatically be dismissed. Instead, look for a lawyer who explains the possible consequences, identifies factual or legal issues that may help the defense, and develops a strategy based on the specific evidence in your case.
ownerUpdates/4/text:
Can A Police Officer Walk Up And Ask Me Questions Without Reasonable Suspicion?

Yes, police may generally approach someone and attempt a consensual encounter without reasonable suspicion. The key issue is whether the encounter actually remains voluntary.

If the officer blocks your departure, issues commands, uses physical force, activates authority in a manner restraining movement, or otherwise creates circumstances in which a reasonable person would not feel free to end the encounter, the interaction may become a detention. At that point, constitutional justification becomes important. Popple v. State provides a major Florida example of how a supposedly limited interaction can become a seizure requiring reasonable suspicion.
ownerUpdates/5/text:
Is Nervousness Enough For Reasonable Suspicion In Florida?

Nervousness can potentially be considered with other facts, but it should not automatically establish reasonable suspicion. Many innocent people become visibly nervous when approached by police, particularly when an officer is armed, uniformed, asking accusatory questions, or standing beside a marked patrol vehicle.

I examine how the officer described the alleged nervousness, whether the behavior was captured on video, what other circumstances existed, and whether the State is relying on nervousness as a substitute for objective evidence. Courts consider the total circumstances, which means the significance of nervous behavior depends heavily on what else occurred.
ownerUpdates/6/text:
Can Police Stop Me Just Because I Look Suspicious?

Generally, an officer needs more than an unsupported statement that someone “looked suspicious” to conduct an investigatory detention. Reasonable suspicion requires articulable circumstances that objectively connect the individual to suspected criminal conduct. Florida courts have repeatedly emphasized that mere suspicion is insufficient for an investigatory stop.

The details therefore matter. An officer who saw conduct closely matching the circumstances of a recently reported offense may have a substantially different legal basis than an officer who simply saw someone standing outside at night. I examine what specific facts the officer knew before the seizure and whether those facts reasonably supported suspected criminal activity.
ownerUpdates/7/text:
What is the difference between petit theft and grand theft in Florida?

The main difference involves the value of the property. Property valued below statutory thresholds generally leads to petit theft charges, while higher-value allegations may result in felony grand theft charges.
ownerUpdates/8/text:
Can I be arrested for theft even if there is no proof?

Yes. Police officers can arrest someone based on probable cause rather than proof beyond a reasonable doubt. That means an accusation, witness statement, or surveillance footage may be enough for an arrest. However, prosecutors still must prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt in court.
ownerUpdates/9/text:
Can a Florida speeding defense attorney get my charge dismissed?

Dismissal may be possible in some cases, but it depends upon the evidence. A defense attorney should not promise dismissal before investigating what occurred. Problems with proof of speed, vehicle identification, evidentiary foundations, witnesses, required statutory elements, or other aspects of the case can sometimes provide grounds for seeking dismissal or prevailing at a contested hearing.
Even when complete dismissal is not realistic, effective representation may still produce a meaningful improvement. I can pursue a reduced charge, reduced penalties, avoidance of incarceration, or another resolution that limits the consequences. The correct strategy depends upon your individual case rather than a predetermined approach.

ownerUpdates/0/text:
October has a way of sneaking up on busy practices.

Before year-end brings new billing codes, updated regulations, and 2027 planning, it's worth asking: has your compliance program kept pace with how your practice has grown this year?

A quick internal review now, checking policies, training records, and reporting channels, can catch gaps before regulators do. Prevention is far less costly than a government inquiry.

Is your program due for a fall check-in?
ownerUpdates/1/text:
Muchos profesionales de salud se quedan callados ante algo que no parece correcto, no porque no les importe, sino porque temen las consecuencias.

La ley protege a quienes reportan de buena fe posibles violaciones a la Ley de Reclamaciones Falsas (False Claims Act), incluyendo protección contra represalias en el trabajo.

Conocer estos derechos, tanto para empleados como para empleadores, construye un ambiente de trabajo más transparente.

Para clínicas y profesionales en Miami, Hialeah y Coral Gables, entender este proceso es el primer paso.

¿Sabías que esta protección existe?
ownerUpdates/2/text:
Many healthcare organizations wait until a regulatory concern arises before reviewing their controlled substance procedures.

Scheduling routine internal reviews helps identify outdated processes, strengthen documentation, and improve consistency before an inspection or audit ever occurs.

A proactive approach supports both patient care and long-term regulatory compliance.

Does your practice conduct regular compliance reviews?
ownerUpdates/3/text:
A strong healthcare compliance program doesn't stop after an audit is complete.

Regular internal reviews, staff education, and billing oversight help healthcare providers identify potential issues early and reduce the likelihood of future Medicare or Medicaid overpayment concerns. Consistency today helps create confidence tomorrow.

How often does your organization review its billing and compliance procedures?
ownerUpdates/4/text:
One of the strongest signs of an effective healthcare compliance program is a workplace where employees feel comfortable asking questions before making difficult decisions.

Open communication helps healthcare providers identify potential concerns early, improve patient care, and reduce regulatory risk. Across Miami, Hialeah, Coral Gables, and throughout Florida, a culture of transparency is one of the best long-term investments a practice can make.

How does your team encourage open communication?
ownerUpdates/5/text:
Protecting your DEA registration isn't just the responsibility of one provider.

From physicians and pharmacists to nurses and administrative staff, every team member contributes to maintaining accurate records, following controlled substance policies, and supporting regulatory compliance.

Building a culture where questions are encouraged helps practices stay prepared and confident every day.

How does your team reinforce compliance?
ownerUpdates/6/text:
Muchas organizaciones cuentan con manuales de cumplimiento que llevan años sin actualizarse.

Revisar políticas internas permite adaptarse a cambios regulatorios, mejorar procesos y ofrecer una guía clara para todo el equipo. Un programa de cumplimiento efectivo evoluciona junto con la práctica médica, no permanece archivado en un estante.

¿Cuál fue la última política que actualizaron en tu organización?
ownerUpdates/7/text:
Las regulaciones cambian, y los equipos también deben mantenerse actualizados.

Capacitar periódicamente al personal sobre políticas internas, documentación y cumplimiento normativo ayuda a prevenir errores que podrían generar investigaciones o sanciones. Una clínica preparada trabaja con mayor confianza y ofrece un mejor servicio a sus pacientes.

¿Cada cuánto tiempo realizan capacitaciones de cumplimiento en tu organización?
ownerUpdates/8/text:
When questions arise during a Medicare or Medicaid audit, organized documentation can help your practice explain billing decisions and demonstrate consistent compliance.

Maintaining complete patient records, accurate coding, and clear internal processes supports both quality care and regulatory readiness. Preparation is often built long before an audit begins.

A former state prosecutor, Jonathan handles DUI, drug charges, theft, assault, domestic violence, traffic offenses, and felony cases. His track record has earned top ratings from Avvo and Martindale-Hubbell, recognition in Florida Trend's Legal Elite, a listing in Cambridge Who's Who in Law, and selection to Florida Super Lawyers. Arrested or charged with a crime in Miami? Call now for a confidential consultation and start building your defense today.
ownerUpdates/0/text: Most Florida drivers facing a first DUI have never been arrested before, and the mistakes they make in the days after the arrest often cause more damage than the arrest itself. A few of the most common: driving on a suspended license, which can add up to 60 days in jail to your case; missing a court date and triggering a bench warrant; and talking about the case with friends, coworkers, or even officers who seem helpful. Anything you say can be used to fill gaps in the prosecution's case. Another major misstep is skipping the police report, since the report is often where a strong defense begins. Many people also waive Miranda rights they did not fully understand, hand evidence to the state through casual conversations, or hire whichever attorney is cheapest rather than one experienced in DUI law. Florida has some of the toughest DUI penalties in the country, and an experienced defense attorney can spot procedural issues, breath test problems, and credibility gaps that may turn the case around.
ownerUpdates/1/text: Being charged with a crime in Florida means making a major decision at arraignment: how you will plead. One option is the no contest plea, also called nolo contendere, a Latin phrase that translates roughly to 'I do not wish to contest.' With a no contest plea you are not admitting that you committed the crime, but you are also not disputing the facts the prosecution has laid out. The court will treat the case as if you were found guilty and move to sentencing. Two things tend to happen next. The case does not go to trial, and the judge schedules a sentencing hearing based on the nature of the offense. Your defense may be able to negotiate a reduced sentence, especially if the prosecutor is willing to consider a plea bargain. The advantage of a no contest plea over a straight guilty plea is that it generally cannot be used against you in a related civil lawsuit. Talk to a Miami criminal defense attorney before entering any plea so you understand the long-term consequences.
ownerUpdates/2/text: Every criminal case is different, and predicting an exact timeline is tough, but Florida cases tend to follow a familiar shape. Misdemeanors typically resolve within about three months. Felonies usually take around six months but can run far longer for serious or complex charges. The process starts at arrest or with a promise to appear in court for lower level offenses. Booking, arraignment, discovery, pretrial motions, and possible plea negotiations all happen before any trial date is set. Felony cases move to circuit court, where discovery should be complete before trial dates are scheduled. Pretrial motions to suppress evidence, compel discovery, or dismiss the case can lengthen the timeline but also reshape the outcome. Cooperation with your defense attorney, quick responses to scheduling, and avoiding new charges all help keep things moving. If your case has stalled and you cannot get answers, a Miami criminal defense lawyer can step in and push it forward.
ownerUpdates/3/text: How long a criminal case takes in Miami-Dade County depends on the charges, the court calendar, and how quickly evidence is exchanged. Some cases resolve in a few months. Complex felonies can stretch beyond a year. The process moves through several stages. After arrest, a bond hearing typically happens within a day or two. Arraignment comes next, where charges are formally read and a plea is entered. Then discovery begins, with both sides exchanging police reports, video, witness lists, and lab results. Defense attorneys often file motions to suppress evidence or challenge investigative procedures, which can pause the case while they are resolved. Plea offers are common at this stage. If the case goes to trial, a misdemeanor trial may last a day or two while a complex felony can run a week or longer. Sentencing usually follows shortly after a conviction. Staying in regular contact with your attorney and responding quickly to requests can keep things moving as efficiently as the system allows.
ownerUpdates/4/text: A Florida DUI conviction is not reported to credit bureaus like a bankruptcy or a judgment, but it can still wreck your credit through the back door. The financial pile-up starts fast. First DUI fines in Florida run between $500 and $2,000, and these cannot be discharged in bankruptcy. Auto insurance premiums often double or triple after a conviction, and an FR-44 financial responsibility certificate is required for three years. Add court costs, DUI school fees, ignition interlock costs, and lost wages from jail or community service, and many people end up putting all of it on credit cards. That balance drives utilization up and the credit score down. Unpaid fines go to collections, which is reported and damages the score further. If a civil judgment is entered against you for damages from a crash, that judgment stays on your credit for seven years whether you pay it or not. The cleanest way to protect your credit is to fight the conviction in the first place.
ownerUpdates/5/text: A common worry after a Florida arrest is whether the charges will follow you forever. The honest answer is that in most cases, yes, unless you take action. Even charges that were dropped or dismissed can remain visible on background checks because arrest records in Florida are public records. A first degree misdemeanor like simple battery or a first DUI conviction stays on your record permanently unless it is sealed or expunged. Felony convictions are generally permanent and ineligible for sealing. Sealing limits who can see the record. Expungement physically removes it from most public databases. Eligibility is narrow: typically you cannot have been adjudicated guilty, and certain offenses such as violent crimes, sex offenses, and DUI convictions are excluded by statute. The process involves a certificate of eligibility from FDLE, a court petition, and proper documentation. Mistakes on the paperwork can delay or kill the application. A defense lawyer can tell you whether you qualify and handle the filing.
ownerUpdates/6/text: Lying to a police officer in Florida is a separate criminal offense, and the consequences reach far beyond the moment. Under Florida Statute 837.05, knowingly giving false information about a crime to law enforcement is a first degree misdemeanor punishable by up to a year in jail, a year of probation, and a $1,000 fine. Giving a false name during a traffic stop, fabricating an alibi during an investigation, or filing a false police report all qualify. The bigger problem is what happens next in your case. Prosecutors and judges treat dishonesty as an aggravating factor, which can mean harsher sentences and fewer plea bargain opportunities. Your credibility takes a hit that follows you into the courtroom. You always have the right to remain silent and ask for an attorney. Using that right is almost always the safer move than improvising answers. If you are facing charges after a statement to police, get legal advice before saying anything further.
ownerUpdates/7/text: If you are placed on probation in Florida for a DUI or any other offense, expect drug and alcohol testing to be part of the deal. Probation officers use a mix of tools, including handheld breath devices, urine tests, hair tests, and PEth blood tests that can detect heavy drinking going back two to three weeks. A positive result might trigger only a warning the first time, but a second positive often becomes a violation of probation, which can mean additional probation, mandatory counseling, or jail time. The frequency of testing is up to the probation officer and varies by case and sobriety history. Even legal substances can create problems if they show up unexpectedly on a panel. The safest path during probation is to avoid alcohol entirely and to be cautious about medications. If you are facing a probation violation hearing after a failed test, a defense attorney can help protect your record and your freedom.
ownerUpdates/8/text: An arrest warrant gives law enforcement legal authority to detain you, and in Florida there are five common situations that trigger one. Failure to appear in court is at the top of the list. Missing a hearing for any reason, even a traffic case, can lead a judge to issue a bench warrant. Probation violations are another frequent trigger, as are new criminal charges built on probable cause from an investigation. Outstanding fines and unpaid child support can also escalate into a contempt warrant. Finally, grand jury indictments can produce a warrant before you ever know you are under investigation. Once a warrant is active, any traffic stop or background check can result in an immediate arrest. That can derail jobs, housing, and travel before the underlying issue is even resolved. If you suspect a warrant has been issued in your name, get legal advice before turning yourself in.
ownerUpdates/9/text: People often use 'hit and run' and 'leaving the scene of an accident' as if they mean different things, but in Florida they describe the same offense. The legal statutes use 'leaving the scene' while the public tends to say 'hit and run.' Either way, the crime is committed when a driver fails to stop after a crash, exchange information, or render aid, regardless of fault. Penalties scale with what happened in the accident. Leaving a property damage crash is a second degree misdemeanor. Leaving a crash involving injury can be charged as a third degree felony with up to five years in prison. Willfully leaving the scene of a fatal accident is a first degree felony carrying up to 40 years and a $10,000 fine. Returning to the scene later does not erase the charge. If you are facing this kind of case in Miami, get a defense lawyer involved before talking to investigators.

Most criminal cases resolve with a negotiated resolution, also called a plea bargain or plea agreement. Your criminal defense attorney and the prosecutor will attempt to work out a resolution so the case does not have to go to trial.

There is a clear incentive for the prosecutor: they avoid bringing in witnesses, burning valuable resources, and carrying out a jury trial. On the defense side, if the evidence is sufficient to convict—thus subjecting the accused to harsh statutory penalties—a well-negotiated plea agreement can result in a significantly reduced sentence.

But the question is—when is the right time to strike a deal? Early in the case? Later on? Somewhere in the middle?

“But Eric, if we invoke my right to remain silent and refuse to provide a statement to the detective, won’t that look bad?”

In times like these, I quote the great Chris Rock:

“What, you wanna look innocent in jail? I'd rather look guilty at the mall."

The detective investigating you is not your friend. 

So what do you care what he thinks?

He probably already thinks you’re guilty. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have his eyes on you.

A detective cannot make an arrest simply because you chose not to speak with them.

If probable cause exists, with or without your statement, they’ll make an arrest.

Invoking your right to remain silent does not mean you’re guilty. 

It means you’re not willing to sit down with a potentially hostile party who is trained in the art of psychological manipulation.

They may not be looking for some “You Can’t Handle the Truth” moment (Gen Z, I’ll give you guys a minute to ask ChatGPT to tell you about “A Few Good Men”).

The detective may be looking for little omissions or slight inconsistencies that, coupled with independent evidence, may infer - at the very least -  that you committed the crime.

What would I want in a criminal attorney if I were charged with a crime:

1) Former PD or former ASA. I believe this experience is invaluable and that this type of experience that cannot be matched in the private sector.

2) Well-known in the county in which my case is located. Do they have good relationships with the prosecutors? Have they practiced before the judge assigned to my case?

3) Stellar reviews.  What do former clients say about this Attorney?

4) Track record of good results.

5) Honest.  Even if they tell me what I don’t want to hear. I don’t want to be sold a lie. Tell me the truth about my case and about likely resolutions.

6) Accessible and responsive (within reason, of course).  If I need to get a hold of them, can I?  Or am I going to be sent to some answering service or some AI menu and maybe they’ll get back to me in a few days?

7) Competent and knowledgeable.  Do they actually know what they’re talking about or are they just pretending?

8) Experience.  They don’t need to have 25 years under their belt, but they need to be more than a rookie.

9) A plan.  What do they want to do to get me the best possible outcome? Or are they just figuring it out as they go along?

10) Competitve fee.  I don’t necessarily need the most expensive lawyer on the planet, but I do not want to bargain shop. This is my life we’re talking about and I’m a firm believer that you get what you pay for.

Appeals in Florida don't re-try your case or bring in new witnesses. Instead, an appellate attorney carefully reviews your entire trial record to spot legal errors that hurt your defense or led to an unlawful sentence. With the words, “We the jury find the defendant not guilty,” Ross Johnson was free to go.

Radjke testified that the cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head, officially stating the manner of death was homicide.

The defendant Ross Johnson took the stand next, with his attorney, David Wheeler from the renown Law Offices of Robert David Malove, working to convince the jury that Johnson was defending his friends.

Prosecutor Mark Graham pushed back against Johnson’s claim that Dayvon Larry was a threat, arguing that he did not hit anybody at any point during the altercation.

Arrested for domestic violence in Miami-Dade? What you do in the first few days matters.

In Florida, a domestic violence arrest usually means staying in jail until a judge sets bond at first appearance. The court will often order no contact with the alleged victim, even if you share a home or children. Many people are surprised to learn that the alleged victim cannot simply drop the charges. That decision belongs to the State Attorney's Office.

The consequences reach well beyond the criminal case. A domestic violence conviction can bar you from owning a firearm under federal law, and it can lead to deportation or loss of status for non-citizens. In Florida, even a withhold of adjudication on a domestic violence charge cannot be sealed. A separate civil injunction can force you out of your home and limit contact with your children.

David Edelstein has defended people accused of domestic violence for more than 30 years, beginning as a Miami-Dade assistant public defender. He handles bond hearings, requests to modify no-contact orders, injunction hearings, and trials. He also advises non-citizens on how a plea will affect their immigration status.

Do not speak to the police or contact the alleged victim before you get legal advice. Call The Edelstein Firm for a confidential consultation.

From Lincoln Road to Collins Avenue, Miami Beach sees heavy foot traffic. Wet lobby floors, pool decks, broken sidewalks and dark parking garages cause serious falls. Florida law requires property owners to keep their premises reasonably safe. If you slip on something like a spilled drink or tracked-in rainwater inside a business, you generally must show the business knew or should have known about it.

That's why evidence matters: photograph the exact spot, get witness names, ask for an incident report and keep the shoes you were wearing.

As a personal injury lawyer Miami Beach residents and visitors can meet in person or by video, Tomas Robirosa will review your case for free. Hablamos español.

Hurt in a crash? The 14-day rule can cost you.

Florida is a no-fault state, so your own Personal Injury Protection (PIP) coverage is usually the first source of payment for medical bills after a car accident. But there's a catch: to use PIP benefits, you generally must get initial medical treatment within 14 days of the crash.

Many people feel fine at first and skip the doctor. Neck, back and head injuries often show up days later, and by then the window may have closed.

Three simple steps: see a doctor promptly, keep every bill and record, and don't give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before getting advice.

Questions about your claim? Speak with a car accident lawyer Miami drivers can reach 24/7 in English or Spanish. The consultation is free.

Call Robirosa Accident & Injury Law at (305) 600-0529.

Storm damage this hurricane season? Don't wait to report it.

We're in the busiest stretch of hurricane season, and even a storm that misses Miami can drive rain through windows, lift roof shingles or back up drains. Under Florida law, you generally have one year from the date of loss to notify your insurer of a new property claim, so the clock matters.

What to do now: photograph every room, keep damaged materials if you can, save repair receipts and write down when you first noticed the problem.

“I have full coverage” doesn't tell you whether you have uninsured motorist protection.

In Florida, uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage may help when an at-fault driver has no bodily injury liability insurance or not enough to cover your injury-related losses. It is different from the coverage that pays to repair your car.

Pull up your policy's declarations page and look for “UM” or “Uninsured Motorist.” Check the limits and whether the coverage is stacked or non-stacked. If the entry is missing or unclear, ask your insurer for the policy and any signed rejection or coverage-selection forms.

After a crash, the policy language and applicable law, not the phrase “full coverage,” determine what coverage may be available.

Medical expenses represent only one piece. Tutoring needs, mental health support, adaptive tools, and disruption to the entire household deserve recognition in any demand.

T Visa vs. U Visa: Know the Difference

Both the T visa and U visa protect crime victims and encourage cooperation with law enforcement, but they're not interchangeable. The T visa is specifically for survivors of human trafficking, while the U visa covers a much broader list of qualifying crimes, including domestic violence and assault. Human trafficking actually qualifies under both, which is where things get confusing. Certification requirements, processing times, and family eligibility also differ between the two. Filing for the wrong one can cost you valuable time. If your situation might involve trafficking or another qualifying crime, an honest case evaluation can point you toward the faster, stronger option. Beyond the legal category, the two visas also differ in whether police involvement is required and how quickly interim protections become available. We're here to help you figure out which path fits, based on what actually happened in your case rather than assumptions.

A new DUI charge and a probation violation are not the same case. They may be related, but they're handled very differently under Florida law.

Your DUI case goes through the criminal court system, where the State must prove the charge beyond a reasonable doubt.

Your probation violation is different. There is no jury, and a judge decides whether a violation occurred using a much lower legal standard.

That means you could successfully defend or even beat the DUI charge and still be found in violation of your probation.

This is why it's critical to understand that you're dealing with two separate legal battles—often moving on different timelines. In many cases, the probation violation can move faster than the new criminal charge.

The sooner you understand the difference, the better prepared you'll be to make informed decisions about your case.

Workers’ compensation in Florida covers a wide range of injuries and illnesses that occur as a result of your job. Covered injuries typically include:

1. Sudden Traumatic Injuries: These are injuries that result from a specific incident at work, such as a slip and fall, a machinery accident, or a car accident while driving for work purposes.

2. Repetitive Motion Injuries: Some injuries develop over time due to the repetitive nature of job duties. Conditions like carpal tunnel syndrome, tendinitis, and back injuries caused by repeated lifting or movement are commonly covered under workers’ compensation.

3. Occupational Illnesses: If your work environment exposes you to harmful chemicals, toxins, or other hazardous conditions that cause illness, you may be entitled to workers’ compensation benefits.

4. Aggravation of a Pre-Existing Condition: If your job duties worsen a pre-existing injury or medical condition, that aggravation may be covered under workers’ compensation, even if the original injury did not occur at work.

5. Injuries That Occur Off-Site: You do not have to be injured at your primary workplace to be covered. If you were injured while performing work duties off-site, you may still be entitled to benefits.

If you are unsure whether your injury qualifies for workers’ compensation benefits, contact our Miami workers’ compensation lawyer today for a free case evaluation.

What does it mean if you receive a federal target letter?

A target letter is a formal notice that federal prosecutors consider you a target of a grand jury investigation. It is not an indictment, an arrest warrant, or a finding of guilt. But it does mean an investigation is well underway, and the decisions made at this stage can shape how the case unfolds.

Federal matters often involve extensive records, multiple agencies, and deadlines that arrive quickly. Having an attorney who understands how federal investigations work can make a real difference in how you're positioned.

Beaton Law Firm defends clients facing federal and state charges from our Coral Gables office. Your consultation is free and confidential.
ownerUpdates/1/text: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon is a third degree felony in Florida, carrying up to five years in prison ⚖️. If the weapon was a firearm, mandatory minimum sentencing kicks in and a judge may have little room to go lighter 🔫. Prior felony convictions can also trigger habitual offender status, which raises the stakes even further and can even lead to life imprisonment in some cases 📈. Florida's self defense law is one of the strongest in the country and does not require you to retreat before using force 🛡️. Our new article breaks down exactly how these charges get built and what defenses actually apply 📖.
ownerUpdates/2/text:
Charged with resisting arrest in Miami? Here's what the prosecution has to prove.

Resisting arrest isn't as automatic as it sounds. Prosecutors have to show specific elements — like whether the officer was engaged in lawful duty and whether your actions actually obstructed that duty — before the charge holds up in court.

This charge often gets added on top of another incident, sometimes when there wasn't a clear violation to begin with. That's exactly why an experienced defense matters early — before assumptions get baked into the case against you.

At Beaton Law Firm, Marcos Beaton brings over two decades of high-level experience to defending clients against these charges throughout Miami and Coral Gables.

ownerUpdates/1/text:
Suffered an injury on a cruise ship but didn't report it to the ship's crew before disembarking? 

It is a common scenario: passengers often feel embarrassed, hope the pain will fade, or just want to enjoy the rest of their vacation. While cruise lines will argue that an unreported incident means it never happened, failing to notify the crew immediately does NOT automatically destroy your legal claim.

Here is how you can still build a strong maritime injury claim:

How to Prove Your Case Without an Onboard Report:

Immediate Home Medical Records: Seeing a doctor right after disembarking links your diagnosis directly to the timing and mechanics of the crash or fall.

Photos & Visuals: Photos of the hazard (wet deck, broken handrail) or of your injuries taken during the trip serve as crucial evidence.

Witness Statements: Fellow passengers or travel companions who saw the accident or helped you afterward can provide sworn statements.

Timestamped Texts: Messages or emails sent to family while onboard serve as powerful contemporaneous proof.

⚠️ Watch Out for Strict Ticket Contract Deadlines!

Unlike standard personal injury claims on land that may give you 2 to 3 years, cruise lines shorten these windows drastically in their fine print. Most major cruise lines require written notice within 6 months and a formal lawsuit filed within 1 year of the injury date.

Don't let tight maritime deadlines or a missing incident report prevent you from seeking justice.
ownerUpdates/2/text:
A excursion booking through your cruise line should be a highlights of your trip—until faulty equipment, an unsafe vehicle, or a careless operator leads to serious injury. When accidents happen off the ship, cruise corporations often claim they bear zero liability because the tour was run by an independent contractor.

Under federal maritime law, corporate disclaimers don't always protect the cruise line.

When Can the Cruise Line Be Held Liable?
If you booked your tour directly through the cruise desk, the cruise line may be responsible for:
📍 Negligent Vetting: Failing to inspect equipment standards or safety histories of foreign operators.
📍 Misrepresentation: Promoting excursions as "safe, official, or hand-selected" while ignoring known safety risks.
📍 Agency Relationships: Exercising significant operational control over the third-party operator.

Strict Maritime Deadlines You Can't Ignore
Cruise ticket contracts carry aggressive fine print designed to limit passenger claims:
⏱️ 6 Months to provide written notice of a personal injury claim.
⏱️ 1 Year statute of limitations to file a formal lawsuit.
⚖️ Mandatory Venue: Most lawsuits must be filed in federal court (typically the U.S. District Court in Miami, FL).

Sustained an Injury or Poor Medical Care on a Cruise Ship?

Many passengers are surprised to learn that most cruise ship doctors are foreign-trained and foreign-licensed. But if medical negligence occurs at sea, does foreign licensing shield the cruise line from a lawsuit?

The short answer: No.

Under current general maritime law:

Equal Standards: Foreign-trained doctors are held to the same objective standard of reasonable care as U.S. medical professionals.

Cruise Line Liability: Cruise lines can be held vicariously liable for the medical mistakes of their onboard staff.

Negligent Hiring: Cruise operators must properly vet, screen, and credential international medical personnel before putting them in charge of passenger safety.

Crucial Advice for Passengers:
Maritime ticket contracts strictly limit your time to take legal action. Most cruise lines enforce a 1-year deadline to file a lawsuit (and require formal written notice within 6 months), typically mandating suits be filed in Miami, Florida.

If you or a loved one suffered harm due to improper treatment, misdiagnosis, or delayed emergency care onboard, act quickly.

Steps to Take Immediately:

Request full copies of your shipboard medical records before disembarking.

Document the names and details of all attending medical staff.

Seek an immediate evaluation at a land-based U.S. hospital.

Consult an experienced cruise ship medical negligence attorney.

Feeling fine after a crash doesn't mean you are — and in Houston, that mistake can cost you more than you think.

Adrenaline masks serious injuries like whiplash, spinal damage, and traumatic brain injuries for hours or even days after a collision. By the time the pain hits, insurance adjusters are already building a case against you — using that gap between your accident and your first doctor's visit to argue your injuries weren't that serious. Texas law can even reduce your compensation if you're found partially at fault for delaying care.

At Amanda Demanda Injury Lawyers, we help Houston accident victims protect both their health and their right to full compensation. If you were hurt in a crash, the steps you take right now matter. ownerUpdates/5/text:
Headaches, confusion, or vision changes after an accident? You may have a TBI—don't wait.

Traumatic brain injuries don't always show up immediately. Symptoms like persistent headaches, memory problems, mood changes and vision issues can appear days or even weeks after a car crash, truck collision, motorcycle accident or slip-and-fall.

Delaying treatment is one of the biggest mistakes TBI victims make. Internal bleeding can silently increase pressure on the brain—and insurance companies will use that delay against your claim.

Amanda Demanda Injury Lawyers has handled a wide range of personal injury cases involving brain injuries. Their team knows how to document your injuries, connect them to the incident, and fight for compensation covering medical bills, lost wages, pain and suffering—including a $43 million car accident jury verdict.

ownerUpdates/6/text:
Road rage isn't an accident. Florida law treats it differently and so do we.

Most car accidents happen because of distraction or a split-second mistake. Road rage is different. When a driver deliberately rams your vehicle, forces you off the road,or follows you to physically confront you, that's not negligence — it's an intentional act.

Florida law recognizes this distinction. Aggressive driving is a traffic violation. Road rage is a criminal offense — covered under assault, battery, and reckless endangerment statutes.

That legal difference matters for your case. When another driver meant to hurt you, the standard insurance claim may not be enough. Intentional torts open the door to punitive damages — compensation specifically designed to punish egregious behavior but proving intent requires a different kind of investigation.

At Amanda Demanda Injury Lawyers, our attorneys know how to build that case. We work with accident reconstruction experts, pull electronic vehicle data, secure dashcam footage and gather witness accounts that establish a pattern of deliberate, targeted conduct.

Road rage behaviors that signal intent:
→ Deliberate ramming or sideswiping
→ Brake-checking to cause a rear-end collision
→ Forcing another vehicle off the road
→ Exiting the vehicle to threaten or attack

If another driver's intentional actions injured you, you deserve representation that matches the seriousness of what happened. Call us for a free consultation.

Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.

What is the true cost of living with a Traumatic Brain Injury?

When a traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs, emergency room treatment is often just the beginning. The financial impact can extend far beyond initial hospitalization—lifetime care costs can range from tens of thousands to over $3 million for severe cases.

Insurance companies frequently focus only on immediate medical bills while ignoring long-term needs. Understanding the full scope of an injury is crucial to securing fair compensation:

• Immediate Medical Needs: Emergency care, neurosurgery, and diagnostic scans.

• Ongoing Care: Inpatient rehabilitation, physical therapy, and cognitive support.

• Hidden Costs: Diminished earning capacity, family caregiving, and home accessibility modifications.

If you or a loved one are facing the long-term impact of a brain injury, don't let insurance companies minimize your recovery.

Hidden Signs: Protecting Your Health After an Accident 

Under state personal injury law, a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) from a car crash or slip-and-fall is fully compensable even if symptoms take days or weeks to appear. Severe mechanical impacts frequently cause a "lucid interval", a period where a victim feels completely fine while microvascular swelling or a subdural hematoma (bleeding on the brain) slowly develops.

Delaying a medical evaluation is the primary metric insurance adjusters use to assert a "gap in treatment" defense to deny high-value brain injury claims. 

Quiet Warning Signs to Watch For

-Cognitive Shifts: Experiencing brain fog, memory lapses, or trouble focusing. This requires neuropsychological mapping to legally document alterations in brain function.

-Sensory Changes: Dealing with sudden light sensitivity, ringing in the ears, or blurry vision. This requires diagnostic imaging (CT/DTI) to provide objective, anatomical proof of trauma.

-Emotional Spikes: Noticing sudden irritability, anxiety, or uncharacteristic mood swings. This requires clinical mental health evaluations to demonstrate the human impact of the injury.

If something feels "off" after a crash, put your health first and see a doctor immediately. Then, call us for a free, compassionate consultation.

ownerUpdates/6/text:
Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.

Before you assume “it wasn’t even a real car,” talk to an experienced DUI lawyer.

Injured in a Lyft in Miami? The insurance company that pays depends on one thing most people never think to check.
Unlike a typical car accident, a Lyft crash doesn't have one clear insurance policy behind it. Coverage depends entirely on what the driver's app status was at the exact moment of the crash — and that difference can mean the gap between a few thousand dollars and up to $1 million in available coverage.
If the driver's app was off, only their personal auto policy applies. If the app was on but they were waiting for a ride request, a smaller contingent policy kicks in. But once a ride is accepted — whether the driver is en route to pick up a passenger or already transporting one — Lyft's $1 million commercial liability policy becomes active.
This distinction matters because Lyft's insurer is not the only party that may investigate your claim. The driver, other involved drivers, and even a vehicle manufacturer in cases involving a defect can all become relevant to determining who is responsible for your injuries.
Florida's comparative negligence law adds another layer: if you're found partially at fault, even as a passenger, it can reduce what you're able to recover. That's why documenting the driver's app status, the crash itself, and your injuries early matters more in a rideshare accident than in a standard car accident case.
If you were hurt in a Lyft accident anywhere in Miami-Dade County, call Bobby Nuñez today.
ownerUpdates/7/text:
Rear-ended in Miami? What happens next isn't as simple as "the other driver is at fault."
Most people assume the driver who hits you from behind is automatically responsible. Under Florida law, that's usually true — but "usually" is where insurance companies find room to work.
Florida's modified comparative negligence law means that if you're found more than 50% at fault for any reason, you can't recover compensation. After a rear-end crash, adjusters look for angles: Did you brake suddenly? Were your brake lights working? Do you have a pre-existing condition they can point to instead of the crash?
There's also a timing issue many victims don't expect. Whiplash, herniated discs, and even traumatic brain injuries can take 24 to 72 hours to show symptoms. Adrenaline masks pain at the scene, so you may feel fine and later develop real injuries the insurance company will try to disconnect from the accident. 
A few things matter most in the first hours after being rear-ended: call 911 so an official report exists, avoid apologizing or admitting fault, photograph the scene before it's cleared, and get evaluated by a doctor the same day, even if you feel okay.

Myth: if you were rear-ended, the claim is automatic and there's nothing to worry about.

Not quite. Fault usually favors you, but the size of your recovery still depends on evidence — camera footage that's often erased within days, the crash report, vehicle damage, and medical records that show the injury is real. Insurers work to chip away at "automatic" cases. Our latest post breaks down exactly what to do after a rear-end crash near the Golden Glades.

Read "Rear-Ended Near the Golden Glades? What Florida Drivers Should Do Next."
ownerUpdates/4/text:
Is the driver who rear-ended me automatically at fault?

Usually — but not automatically. Florida expects drivers to leave enough room to stop, so the driver behind often bears most of the blame. But insurers routinely argue the front driver stopped short or changed lanes late, because under Florida's comparative-negligence rule any share of fault pinned on you reduces your recovery. That's why even a "clear" rear-end crash on NE 163rd Street or near the Golden Glades is worth having a lawyer look at. The consultation is free and you pay nothing unless we win.

ownerUpdates/5/text:
Key fact: after a crash in North Miami, more than one insurance policy may pay — and they stack in a specific order.

Your own PIP covers part of your medical bills and lost wages no matter who was at fault, if you're treated within 14 days. The at-fault driver's bodily-injury coverage answers for the rest — and if they had none, your uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage can step in, which matters on corridors like Biscayne Boulevard where uninsured drivers are common. Sorting out which policy pays first is half the battle.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Yes, you can get a DUI in Florida without driving a car.

Many people assume DUI charges only happen behind the wheel of a car or truck, but Florida law is much broader. You can be arrested for DUI while operating a motorcycle, golf cart, scooter, bicycle, lawn mower, or even a boat in some situations.

Florida focuses on whether you were in “actual physical control” of a vehicle while impaired, not just whether you were driving down I-95.

That means a bad decision on a golf cart in your neighborhood or riding a mower home after a few drinks can turn into a serious criminal case with fines, license issues, and a permanent record.
